info.title: VulnerableAPI Demo API
info.description:
An intentionally vulnerable Spring Boot API for Fortify security scanning, security training, and controlled API testing. It includes user and account lookups, demo login and encryption, fund transfers, file access, URL fetching, redirects, command execution, XML parsing, and Java object deserialization.

**Warning: This application is intentionally insecure. Never expose it to public or untrusted networks or use real credentials, sensitive data, or untrusted inputs.** Requests execute real operations and may change demo balances, read server files, make outbound requests, or run server-side commands.

Each operation describes its intentional vulnerability, parameters, test defaults, and environment requirements. To test accounts, call /login with alice/password, copy the plain-text token into Authorize, and request /accounts/bob. Tokens expire after one hour or an app restart. The other endpoints remain public. Authentication intentionally does not prevent cross-account access.

post.summary: Parse XML - XML external entity injection
post.description: Intentionally uses default XML parser settings without disabling external entities, demonstrating XXE. Returns the root element's text content. The example is valid, harmless XML; a declaration or comment without a root element is invalid. Malformed XML currently returns 500.

requestBody.description: Complete XML document with one root element; its text content is returned.

post.description: Intentionally omits positive-amount validation and sender authorization. The default transfers 100 from alice to bob and changes real demo balances. An amount of -100 reverses the balance updates, crediting the sender. Repeated positive transfers may fail when the sender has insufficient funds.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Sender account username whose balance is debited.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Recipient account username whose balance is credited.

parameters.name: amount
parameters.description: Decimal amount to transfer; negative values intentionally reverse the transfer.

post.summary: Demo login - log forging and weak credentials
post.description: Intentionally logs the username without sanitizing line breaks, allowing forged log entries. Also demonstrates MD5 password hashing, hard-coded admin credentials, and predictable Random-based tokens. The defaults log in as seeded alice. Copy the plain-text response into Swagger's Authorize dialog without the Bearer prefix. API clients send `Authorization: Bearer TOKEN` to /accounts. Tokens expire after one hour and are lost on restart; no browser session cookie is created.

parameters.name: username
parameters.description: Username to authenticate; also written verbatim to the application log.

parameters.name: password
parameters.description: Demo password for the selected user; alice's seeded password is password. Sent as a query parameter, so do not use a real password.

post.description: Intentionally encrypts using DES in ECB mode with a hard-coded key. Returns Base64 ciphertext. This is a weak-cryptography demo, not suitable for real secrets.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: Plaintext to encrypt using the intentionally weak demo cipher.

post.summary: Read a serialized object - insecure deserialization
post.description: Intentionally deserializes untrusted bytes with ObjectInputStream without an object filter. Only upload a trusted test object. Returns Deserialized: java.lang.String for a serialized String. Ordinary text, XML, JSON, and ZIP files are not Java object streams and currently cause 500. Browsers cannot preselect a local file, so this input requires manual selection.

requestBody.description: Binary file produced by Java ObjectOutputStream.writeObject(), sent as the raw body, not multipart form data. For a harmless sample, run in jshell: try (var out = new java.io.ObjectOutputStream(new java.io.FileOutputStream("sample.ser"))) { out.writeObject("Hello from Swagger"); } Then select sample.ser below.

get.description: Intentionally concatenates the supplied name into SQL without parameterization. The default looks up the seeded alice user; modified input can change the query.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Username to look up in the seeded users table.

get.summary: Redirect to a URL - open redirect
get.description: Intentionally redirects to an unvalidated target with HTTP 302. The relative default stays on this server so Swagger can follow it. External destinations may show Failed to fetch because the browser enforces CORS after the redirect; use normal browser navigation or a client that does not follow redirects to inspect the 302.

parameters.name: target
parameters.description: Relative or absolute destination URL placed in the redirect Location header.

get.description: Intentionally inserts the host into a command executed by sh -c without escaping. The default pings loopback once. Requires sh and ping on the server and permission to send ICMP; minimal containers may not support this. Only use trusted inputs.

parameters.name: host
parameters.description: Hostname or IP address passed to the server's ping command.

get.summary: Render a greeting - reflected cross-site scripting
get.description: Intentionally writes the name directly into HTML without output encoding, demonstrating reflected XSS. The default produces a harmless greeting. Swagger displays response content; it does not reproduce all behavior of navigating to the HTML page.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Name inserted verbatim into the HTML greeting.

get.description: Intentionally combines the supplied name with app.files.base-dir without checking that the result stays inside that directory. Reads files from the server, not your browser. Startup creates sample.txt without overwriting existing content. Missing or unreadable files currently produce 500 because file-read exceptions are not handled.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: File path relative to app.files.base-dir (default /tmp/vulnapp-files); sample.txt is created at startup.

get.summary: Fetch a URL - server-side request forgery
get.description: Intentionally opens a user-supplied URL from the server without restricting destinations or protocols, demonstrating SSRF. The default fetches example.com and requires outbound HTTPS and DNS access from the server. Only request destinations you are authorized to test.

parameters.name: url
parameters.description: Absolute URL fetched by the server; its response is returned as text.

get.description: Intentionally checks only that a Principal exists, not that it owns the requested account. An authenticated alice can request bob's email and balance. First call /login, then paste its plain-text token into Swagger's Authorize dialog. API clients send `Authorization: Bearer TOKEN`. Missing, invalid, or expired tokens return 401. Tokens expire after one hour or an app restart.

parameters.name: username
parameters.description: Account owner to look up; seeded owners are alice, bob, and carol.

bearerAuth.description: Paste the plain-text token returned by POST /login, without the Bearer prefix. Demo tokens expire after one hour or an app restart and use intentionally weak randomness.
